easy.def: Something you are very good at.
examples: She has a talent for singing.
Drawing is his talent.
We will have a talent show.

more.def: A natural ability to do something well.
examples: His talent for drawing was clear even when he was little.
She showed her talent at the piano concert.
He has a real talent for making people laugh.
The soup is tasty.
This is a tasty apple.
Dad made a tasty lunch.
Grandpa makes a tasty vegetable stew.
The market sells tasty fresh bread.
Add some herbs to make the sauce more tasty.

easy.def: A tool that makes far away things look big.
examples: I saw the moon with a telescope.
The telescope is on a stand.
He looked at a ship with a telescope.

more.def: A tool you look through that makes distant things, like stars, appear larger and closer.
examples: Through the telescope, we could see the rings of Saturn.
The sailor spotted land through his telescope.
A huge telescope on the mountain studies distant stars.

easy.def: How hot or cold something is.
examples: The temperature is cold today.
What is the temperature outside?
The nurse took my temperature.

more.def: A measure of how hot or cold something is.
examples: The temperature dropped below freezing, and the pond turned to ice.
Bake the cake at a low temperature.
The temperature of the ocean is rising.
I had a terrible dream.
The milk smells terrible.
I have a terrible cold.
A terrible storm knocked out the power for two days.
The roads were in terrible shape after the flood.
He felt terrible about forgetting her birthday.

easy.def: The loud boom you hear in a storm.
examples: The thunder was so loud!
The dog hides when it hears thunder.
Thunder comes after lightning.

more.def: The loud rumbling sound that follows a flash of lightning.
examples: The thunder rattled the windows of the house.
We heard thunder rolling in the distance.
Our dog hides under the bed whenever there is thunder.
My room is tidy now.
Keep your desk tidy.
She has tidy hair.

more.def: Neat, with everything in its proper place.
examples: He keeps his desk tidy so he can find things easily.
The garden had tidy rows of beans.
His handwriting is small and tidy.
An ant is tiny.
The baby has tiny toes.
A tiny bug sat on my hand.
A tiny seed can grow into a giant tree.
There was a tiny crack in the glass.
The kitten was so tiny that it fit in my hand.

easy.def: A storm with wind that spins very fast.
examples: The tornado spun across the field.
We go to the basement in a tornado.
The tornado looked like a big gray cone.

more.def: A powerful storm with a spinning, funnel-shaped column of wind.
examples: The family hid in the basement until the tornado passed.
The tornado tore the roof off the barn.
A siren warns the town when a tornado is near.

easy.def: Something a family or group does again and again over many years.
examples: It is our tradition to bake a cake on birthdays.
Our tradition is to eat pancakes on Sunday.
It is a tradition to sing that song.

more.def: A belief or way of doing things that is passed down in a family or group over time.
examples: It is a tradition in her family to tell stories around the fire every winter.
The school has a tradition of planting a tree every year.
By tradition, the oldest child lights the candles.

easy.def: Clear, so you can see through it.
examples: Glass is transparent.
The fish tank is transparent.
A transparent bag lets you see inside.

more.def: Clear enough that you can see through it.
examples: The jellyfish was almost transparent in the water.
Tape the transparent plastic over the window.
The water was so transparent that we could see the bottom.

easy.def: To go from one place to another.
examples: We travel to the beach by car.
We travel by bus.
Birds travel far in the fall.

more.def: To go from one place to another, often over a long distance.
examples: They traveled across the country by train.
Light travels faster than sound.
My aunt travels to many countries for her job.

easy.def: Gold, gems, or other special things.
examples: The pirates hid the treasure.
The map shows where the treasure is.
My rock is a treasure to me.

more.def: Valuable things such as gold and jewels, or something very special to you.
examples: The divers found treasure in the sunken ship.
The museum's greatest treasure is a golden mask.
Grandma's letters are a treasure to our family.
My hands tremble when I am cold.
The puppy trembled in the cold.
My voice trembles when I am scared.

more.def: To shake slightly because you are cold, afraid, or excited.
examples: The leaves trembled in the gentle wind.
The ground trembled as the train passed.
His hands trembled as he opened the letter.

easy.def: To feel sure that someone is good and honest.
examples: I trust my mom.
I trust my friend to keep a secret.
The dog trusts me.

more.def: To believe that someone is honest and will not hurt you or let you down.
examples: You can trust her to keep a promise.
Do you trust the weather report?
It takes time to trust someone new.
